questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A tailor keeps tins of petrol in his shop although his insurance policy forbids it. The stored petrol is regarded in insurance as a
questions.explanation: It raises the chance that fire will strike.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The person named in a life insurance policy to receive the money when the insured person dies is the
questions.explanation: The payout is his when the policy matures in death.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A dealer buys shares in Lagos in the morning and sells the same shares the same day in another market where the price is higher, gaining from the price difference. This practice is
questions.explanation: Two prices, one quick profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Shares of large, old and financially sound companies, known for steady dividends and safety, are nicknamed
questions.explanation: The safest names on the exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A flour miller sells wheat forward at a fixed price while the wheat is still growing, so that a fall in price before harvest cannot ruin him. This protective dealing is
questions.explanation: The deal today shields him from tomorrow.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A speculator on the stock exchange who has promised to buy shares but cannot raise the money when settlement is due, and so fails, is called a
questions.explanation: He waddles out of the market wounded.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The document, like a cheque, which a company sends to a shareholder to pay him his dividend is a
questions.explanation: He takes it to the bank and is paid.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The steel drawer fitted into a bank's outer wall, into which a trader can drop his money bag after banking hours, is the
questions.explanation: The bank is shut, but the slot still receives.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The small part of a cheque left in the cheque book after the cheque is torn out, on which the payment is recorded, is the
questions.explanation: It stays behind as the drawer's own record.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The small book in which a savings-customer's deposits and withdrawals are written and stamped each time he visits the bank is the
questions.explanation: The bank and the customer each see the story.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Alhaji sends forty bags of cement by road to his customer in Kaduna, and the customer is to pay after receiving them. The person to whom the goods are sent is the
questions.explanation: The goods travel to him, not from him.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Where big ships cannot berth close to the quay, goods are carried to and from them in small flat-bottomed boats. The service is called
questions.explanation: Small boats bridge ship and shore.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The smallest number of members that must be present at a meeting before any business done there is valid is the
questions.explanation: Without that number the meeting cannot decide.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A shareholder who cannot attend the company's annual meeting fills a form authorising another member to attend and vote in his place. The authorised person is a
questions.explanation: He carries the absent member's vote.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: When votes at a shareholders' meeting are equal for and against a motion, the chairman gives a second and deciding vote. This vote is his
questions.explanation: It breaks the tie at the table.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The one-off meeting which a public limited company must hold shortly after it is permitted to commence business is the
questions.explanation: The law itself requires it once.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A meeting called between annual meetings because an urgent matter, such as removing a director, cannot wait for the next AGM, is an
questions.explanation: Business too urgent to keep for a year.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The officer of a company, appointed by the directors, who keeps the company's records, sends out notices of meetings and files statutory returns is the
questions.explanation: The company's memory and its messenger.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The list of items of business, arranged in the order in which they will be discussed, that members receive before a meeting, is the
questions.explanation: It tells the meeting where to begin and end.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A filing system in which folders lie flat in a drawer, one upon another, so that the papers are stored in piles rather than on edge, is
questions.explanation: The files sleep in stacks inside the drawer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The guide, alphabetical or numerical, kept so that any needed file in the cabinet can be located quickly, is called
questions.explanation: Follow the guide and the file is found.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A clerk files Mr Okoro's papers under 'Okoro' and places a card under 'Chukwu' saying 'see Okoro'. The card he has placed is a
questions.explanation: It points from one name to another.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The system of rapid writing in special signs and shortened strokes, used by clerks and secretaries to record speech as it is spoken, is
questions.explanation: The pen keeps pace with the speaker.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The office machine that makes exact paper copies of an existing document, page by page, at the touch of a button, is the
questions.explanation: One page in, many identical pages out.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Advertising signs made of glass tubes that glow with coloured light at night, common above shops and bars, are
questions.explanation: The gas in the tube glows when switched on.
